title: Pasta alla Checca
subtitle: No-cook fresh tomato and basil sauce with spaghetti
excerpt: Cherry tomatoes marinated with garlic, basil, and olive oil, then tossed with hot spaghetti. No hob required for the sauce. A summer dish that is ready in the time it takes to cook the pasta.
sourceNotes: Roman home cooking tradition. Alla checca refers to the raw, uncooked tomato sauce that is a signature of central Italian summer cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the tomatoes up to 2 hours ahead at room temperature. Do not refrigerate or the tomatoes will lose flavour.

content.text: Pasta alla checca is a no-cook Roman sauce of ripe cherry tomatoes, basil, and olive oil. It gives a bright, fresh dish that needs nothing more than good tomatoes and hot pasta. Use the ripest tomatoes you can find.
Put the halved cherry tomatoes, garlic, half the basil, and olive oil into a large bowl. Season with salt and black pepper.
Toss everything together and leave at room temperature for at least 30 minutes. Do not refrigerate.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the spaghetti according to the packet until al dente.
Reserve a cup of pasta cooking water before draining.
Drain the pasta and add it immediately to the bowl with the tomatoes. Toss quickly and well.
Add a splash of pasta water if the sauce seems dry. Toss again until the pasta is well coated.
Scatter the remaining basil over the top. Add the mozzarella, parmesan, and chilli flakes if using. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The sauce tastes dull and flat.
items.cause: The tomatoes were underripe or the marinating time was too short.
items.fix: Use the ripest tomatoes available. Leave the sauce for at least 30 minutes so the salt draws out the juices.

items.symptom: The pasta is stodgy and clumped.
items.cause: The pasta was not tossed with the sauce immediately after draining.
items.fix: Drain the pasta and toss it with the sauce while it is still very hot. Add pasta water to loosen if needed.

items.symptom: The garlic tastes too sharp and raw.
items.cause: The garlic was sliced too thickly or the marinating time was short.
items.fix: Slice the garlic very fine next time so it softens in the oil and tomato juice. A longer marinating time will also mellow it.
